label: digit 0 input at original position 0 or 1
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 0 at one of the first two original-phase steps (t=0 or t=1); every such step activates (precision 1.0). At t=0 activation is a constant ~0.54 of max; at t=1 magnitude depends on the preceding first token (max 1.0 after y, ~0.44-0.52 after d/u, near zero when the first token was also 0). Weak residual firing (~0.04-0.2 of max, about 1% of mass) on a 0 at t=2. Never fires on any other token, on 0 at t>=3, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase.

issues: The explanation makes a false magnitude claim. It says the t=1 activation is 'near zero when the first token was also 0'. In fact, a 0 at t=1 right after a 0 at t=0 fires on all 584 test cases (predicate (in_tok==0)&(t==1)&(prev_tok==0) has precision 1.0) at about 0.82 of max. Misses output shows this every time, e.g. '[0:0.54] [0:0.82] w <DEL>'. That is one of the larger activation levels, not near zero.

The predicate and label hold up. Test precision is 1.0, recall 0.949, F1 0.974 and mass recall 0.99, with zero false positives. The feature never fires on non-0 tokens, on the delimiter, in the copy phase, or at t>=3.

The t=2 leftover is non-systematic and small, as described: about 11% of 0 inputs at t=2 fire (precision 0.109), weakly (0.04-0.25 of max), holding about 1% of mass. Requiring no earlier 0 does not separate those cases (precision 0.109). Adding t=2 to the predicate drops test F1 to 0.836, so the original predicate is the better one.
The other magnitude claims check out: t=0 is a constant 0.54 of max, after y it reaches 1.00, after u it is about 0.52 and after d about 0.44.
